newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine pension fund won't rule out acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Argentine pension fund won't rule out acquisition.

text.p: Origenes AFJP, Argentina's largest private pension fund, does not rule out the possibility of buying up other funds, the firms' president said.
"Our idea is size so we are not buying anything but I don't think we are ruling out for the future," Origenes President Guillermo Alchouron told Reuters.
Origenes purchased the Activa-Anticipar pension fund a couple of weeks ago for $110 million, making it the largest Argentine fund in terms of members. It will now manage $600 million in funds.
Alchouron said "if another fund turns up that looks as good as Activa-Anticipar with its sound finances, we would have no problems buying it."
Origenes is owned 51 percent by Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires and 49 percent by Spanish banking group Santander.
"The problem is not just that of Origenes, but at the moment all of our colleagues, especially the industry leaders, are thinking of absorbing some other smaller fund," said Alchouron.
Analysts say the ongoing streamlining of Argentina's private pension fund system is set to continue because of the benefits of economies of scale in offering better services to clients.
Gary Becker, the winner of the 1992 Nobel Prize in economics said this week he expected the number of funds to decline to 15 from the current 21.
The five largest private pension firms manage some 60 percent of the funds in the pensions market.
